"The Way of Men" is a 2012 book by Jack Donovan, an antifeminist Spearhead writer. Within the text, Donovan presents a convincing explanation on the origin of gender roles. Essentially, Donovan explains the "gender ethos" as a method of encouraging men and women to perform the tasks that they are most biologically equipped for. To explore this argument, Donovan asks us to consider a small group of humans surviving alone in the wilderness. (slightly edited) From the text:

"To thrive, humans need protein and fat. You can get enough protein and fat from vegetables, but without an established farm you're going to be hard pressed to gather enough vegetables to meet your nutritional needs. A large animal can provide protein and fat for days, longer if you know how to preserve the meat.

The problem with big, protein-rich animals is that they don't want to die... They're going to fight for their lives. Taking down a big, protein-rich animal is going to be dangerous. It will require strength, courage, technique, and teamwork. Finding food also requires exploring, venturing out into the unknown...

If you are going to survive, your group will need protection from predators... If there is someone or something out there who wants what you have and is willing to fight for it, you're going to need to figure out who in your group is going to be willing to fight back. You'll want the people who are best at fighting to stand watch, to defend everything you care about, or to go out and eliminate a potential threat. If someone or something has something that you need, the best way to get it may be to take it. Who in your group will be willing and able to do that?

If females are with you, they won't have access to reliable birth control. Males and females won't stop having sex, and females will get pregnant. Humans are mammals, and like most mammals, a greater part of the reproductive burden will fall on women. That's not fair, but nature isn't fair. Even strong, aggressive women become more vulnerable and less mobile during pregnancy. Even tough women will nurse their young. They'll bond with their offspring and take to caring for them quickly. Babies are helpless, and children are vulnerable for years.

If there were no other physical or mental differences between women and men, in a hostile environment the biological realities of human reproduction would still mean that over time more men would be charged with exploring, hunting, fighting, building, and defending. Men would have more time to specialize and develop the necessary skills to excel at those tasks. They wouldn't have a good excuse not to.

Men will never get pregnant, they will never be nursing, and they will be less encumbered by their children. They may not even know who their children are. Women know who their kids are. Children don't depend on their fathers in the same way that they depend on their mothers. Men are freer to take risks for the good of the group, believing that their offspring will live on.

As things are, there are biological differences between men and women that have little to do with pregnancy or breastfeeding. On average, men are bigger and stronger than women. Men are more daring, probably more mechanically inclined, and generally better at navigating. Men are hard wired for aggressive play. High testosterone men take more risks and seek more thrills. Men are more interested in competing for status, and when they win, their bodies give them a dopamine high and more testosterone.

Because your group is struggling to survive, every choice matters. If you give the wrong person the wrong job, that person could die, you could die, another person could die, or you could all die. Because of the differences between the sexes, the best person for jobs that involve exploring, hunting, fighting, building, or defending is usually going to be a male. This is not some arbitrary cultural prejudice; it is the kind of vital strategic discrimination that will keep your group alive.

The practical division of labor is where the male world begins."
Jack Donovan's "The Way of Men" and the Origin of Gender Roles

Here a text-version of the comment, which might be easier to read of a mobile device.

Yes, I do. In addressing this (and I know this is not really the right forum here but I don't make many statements about this anywhere), I don't want to speak too much from a position of male privilege. I am however, a member of a minority group and have at least some experience with discrimination, racism, etc, both overt and subtle.

As much as some would like to change things by fiat or highly dynamic means (I use that work instead of "violence" since there is a real violence in the world, and then there's internet violence, which is real but different), I don't think that's the way true, long-term change is effected.

Feminism is over 100 years old. It is still a work in progress. But it has made its gain steadily over the decades by winning over hearts and minds, through education and cogent argument. Yes, some of it is legislation. But legislation (especially in the U.S.) requires first the educating and convincing of other minds. It is a slow process. But it works, and it is the real, true solution - an evolution of culture and mindset that has real staying power. I believe, ultimately, in the slow but inevitable power of Gandhi's satyagraha, loosely translation as "insistence on truth," but more easily understood as "the irresistible power of truth."

And for the truth to be expressed, beheld, and eventually accepted - that requires real open discourse. Yes, this takes time. But as I mentioned, I am in no rush - I am devoted to reddit's long-term success. As a city-state, reddit is also a reflection of internet culture - one that has a way a go in terms of evolution. We can't stamp out ideas we don't like by erasing them. They don't really go away. You can only change them, through showing, explaining, demonstrating the truth.

Yes, it is unfair. The task of convincing others is harder on the satyagrahi, they are the ones who bear the responsibility of argument, of debate, of explication. But still it must be done. Misogyny, sexism. Racism. Homophobia. Transphobia. And things I've forgotten about because they've slipped my mind due to my privilege.

This is why I will uphold freedom of speech. Because waht is right and what is truth can only, ultimately, win this way.

So I would say, roughly:

1) Continue your stuggle. Culture is changed by patient education, by explaining, by building empathy, by showing others what you know to be true. I know that reddit is a place for that.

When I was 13 or 14, I was on a BBS somewhere, and in some discussion I used the word "fag," because it was a popular insult for young teen boys. The sysop of the BBS, who turned out to be a lesbian who worked at ConAgra (I don't know why I remember this particular fact) chatted me and told me in quite a friendly but firm way that that word was a slur against gay people, it was very offensive, and I should not use it again. I learned that day, and I was ashamed of what I'd done, and that has always stuck with me since.

Much is done in ignorance, and the only antidote is education. I'm sure you've seen the post/thread about the Sikh woman. That is the kind of thing I'm talking about. The OP in that thread will forever remember what he learned, he will tell others what he learned, and the change in him will ripple outwards to the world. It will be a permanent change, the change that comes from understanding.

2) Continue to build and maintain women-friendly (and gay-friendly, and trans-friendly) spaces on reddit. This too has its analogue in the offline world. Women need and have woman-friendly safe spaces and this attracts other women, makes them feel welcome and secur, and builds a place for them. Promote them to other women who want to enjoy what reddit has to offer.

Eventually this builds into a critical mass, the the weight of institutional or cultural biases can be addressed on an equal footing. This too is how society has changed. You can't always debate effectively when you're outnumbered, but if you have an enclave you can build your numbers and develop your ideas, created an alternative society, and then present it to the mainstream as a new direction. Even reddit itself is like this.
